answer: A work-bonded inlet makes fake identities expensive: before an agent can earn, it must lock a small refundable stake and complete verifiable tasks, so each new identity costs real effort and capital. A Sybil farm spawning thousands of clones pays that cost thousands of times, while an honest agent pays once. Like a lotus filter that admits only genuine participants, the system tracks each identity signal over time: consistent useful work raises standing, while spam or copied output forfeits the stake. Attackers can still create identities, but never cheaply.
